messages.subject: encoding handling?
parts:
Hi! I had quite the adventure with knitr today, when I found that
things were working differently when I ran them in Rstudio (as normal)
as compared to running them as part of knitting to HTML. After much
futzing around, I found the problem was an en dash in one of my input
files, which read into R just fine with "read.csv('filename.txt')" but
when running that during the knit, the file quit loading precisely at
the en dash (octal \226, emphatically NOT a regular ASCII hyphen). Are
the encoding assumptions inside the knitting environment different
somehow? It seems, from my fairly ignorant position, that it would be
nice to have things work when knitting exactly as they do when
otherwise using R. Is there a reason for this behavior, or some
setting that I ought to be setting anyway, or something like that?
Thanks for all the awesomeness of knitr,

- Aaron

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] encoding handling?
parts:
Encoding is always a pain under the OS which does not use UTF8
consistently (aka Windows). Your Rnw or Rmd file has its own encoding,
and the CSV file seems to have another type of encoding. RStudio
respects the encoding of your source file, but the CSV file is really
out of its control (there is no reliable way to detect the encoding of
a file automatically).

A similar issue has been brought forward before:
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/256#issuecomment-5938451

Or see the fileEncoding/encoding arguments in ?read.csv

Regards,
Yihui
